optional.note: Fresh or frozen pandan leaves both work.

tools.name: Bowl
tools.note: Use a heatproof bowl for soaking the chilies.

tools.name: Fine sieve
tools.note: Used for rinsing the rice and the anchovies.

tools.name: Blender
tools.note: Used to make the sambal paste.

tools.name: Saucepan
tools.note: A medium size works best, and a heavy base helps prevent scorching.

tools.name: Pot
tools.note: Any pot of similar size will work for boiling the eggs.

tools.name: Frying pan
tools.note: A small size is useful here, but a medium pan can be used instead.

tools.name: Slotted spoon
tools.note: A regular spoon or a pair of tongs can stand in.

tools.name: Wooden spoon
tools.note: A silicone or metal spoon also works for stirring.

steps.title: Prep and blend the chili paste
points: Do all the prep first.
Snip the stems off the dried chilies and shake out most of the seeds.
Put the chilies in the heatproof bowl, pour the boiling water over them, and soak for 20 minutes.
While they soak, rinse the rice in the sieve until the water runs clear, then set it aside to drain.
Rinse the anchovies in the sieve and pat them completely dry with paper towels.
Peel and roughly chop the shallots and garlic.
Peel the onion and slice it into thin rings.
Slice the cucumber into rounds.
Drain the chilies, keeping 1/4 cup of the soaking liquid.
Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic, shrimp paste, and reserved liquid into a smooth paste.

steps.title: Cook coconut rice
points: Put the rice, coconut milk, water, salt, pandan leaves, and ginger in the saucepan and stir once.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, then cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Take the pan off the heat and let it rest, still covered, for 10 minutes.
Remove the pandan and ginger and fluff the rice with a fork.

steps.title: Boil and peel eggs
points: While the rice cooks, bring the medium pot of water to a boil.
Lower in the eggs with the slotted spoon and simmer for 9 minutes.
Move them to the bowl of cold water, then peel and halve them.

steps.title: Fry peanuts and anchovies
points: Heat the 1/2 cup of oil in the small frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the peanuts for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until the skins darken and the nuts smell toasted.
Lift them out onto the lined plate.
Fry the anchovies in the same oil for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until golden and crisp.
Lift them out onto the plate.

steps.title: Cook the chili paste
points: Heat the 1/4 cup of oil in the large frying pan over medium-low heat.
Add the chili paste and cook for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until it turns a deep brick red and the oil separates from the paste.
Add the onion rings and cook for 5 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the tamarind paste, sugar, and salt, and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in a quarter of the fried anchovies.

steps.title: Plate the dish
points: To serve, put a mound of coconut rice on each plate.
Arrange a spoonful of sambal, some of the remaining anchovies and peanuts, two egg halves, and a few cucumber slices around it.

troubleshooting.problem: The sambal tastes raw and sharp
troubleshooting.solution: It was not cooked long enough. Keep cooking over medium-low heat until the oil visibly pools at the edges of the paste.

troubleshooting.problem: The rice scorches on the bottom or turns gummy
troubleshooting.solution: Coconut milk sticks easily. Use a heavy saucepan, keep the heat low once it boils, and do not lift the lid or stir during cooking.

troubleshooting.problem: The anchovies come out chewy or the oil spatters
troubleshooting.solution: Dry them thoroughly after rinsing. Wait until a test anchovy sizzles at once before adding the rest.

troubleshooting.problem: The peanuts taste burnt once they cool
troubleshooting.solution: Take them out when they are just golden inside, not dark brown. They keep cooking after leaving the pan.
